This working directory appears to be empty (no files found), so I can't inspect the actual `misc`/`utils` contents here — I'll work from your description, but the concrete file listing would let me finalize exact placements rather than guess.

**Proposed disposition rules** (apply each file in `misc`/`utils` against these — every file needs to satisfy exactly one):

| Current dumping-ground content | Where it goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Config templates | `config/templates/` (or per-service `<service>/config/` if only one consumer) | Has a clear single purpose; earn its own home |
| One-off migration scripts (already run) | `scripts/migrations/archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<description>/` | Historical record, not active tooling — separate from scripts still in use |
| Archived compliance reports | Probably **not the code repo at all** — move to your document/compliance system (Drive, Confluence, etc.), or if they must stay, `docs/compliance/archive/` with a README stating retention policy | Reports aren't code; keeping them in-repo just recreates the dumping-ground problem |
| Shared helpers used by 2 services | Promote to a real shared package: `libs/shared/<name>/` or `packages/shared-<name>/` with its own README and tests | It has a real multi-consumer contract — it's "earned" its own module, unlike single-use utils |
| Old meeting notes | Delete from repo, or move to wiki/Drive | Not code, not a build artifact — has no reason to live in the codebase |
| `utils/` grab-bag (~30 files) | No replacement `utils` folder. Each file either: (a) used by exactly one service → move into that service's own `utils/` or `internal/` subfolder, (b) used by 2+ services → promote to `libs/<domain>/` (e.g. `libs/dates/`, `libs/strings/`), (c) unused → delete | A generic `utils` is banned by design — it has no single reason to change, so it always regrows into a dumping ground |

**Top-level shape this produces:**
```
libs/            # promoted, multi-consumer shared code, one subfolder per concern
  shared/<name>/
  dates/
scripts/
  migrations/
    archive/
config/
  templates/
docs/
  compliance/archive/   # only if it truly must live in-repo
<service-a>/
  internal/utils/       # single-service-only helpers, co-located
<service-b>/
  internal/utils/
```

Each non-trivial folder above gets a short README stating its purpose and what belongs there, so it doesn't silently become the next `misc`.

**Before I finalize:** can you share the actual file listing (or a directory tree) of `misc` and `utils`? I want to sort every one of the ~77 files into a bucket rather than leave anything ambiguous, and flag any that don't cleanly fit one of these rules for your call.
